title: Release 1.24.0: OpenRouter adapter and strict ship checks
head: lessons-177-178
body:
## Summary

Release 1.24.0 adds the OpenRouter adapter and closes ship-check gaps from field lessons 177–179, 181, and 183.

- OpenRouter requests enforce data-collection denial, provider pinning for Anthropic models, bookkeeping-only outputs for DeepSeek models, priced request limits, per-job and daily spend caps, and coordinator-owned spend records.
- Ship can derive supported checks from CI, warn about hand-written checks that differ, and identify failures reproduced on the base tree. Optional CI retries apply only when the failing tests are outside the changed files.
- Test-file guards inspect added lines. Explicit exemptions require a reason and appear in the audit log and PR body.
- Binary resolution rejects directories and reports launch errors clearly.
- A missing Node lockfile produces `no-lockfile: <path>/package.json has no package-lock.json` and explicitly says the npm lock check did not run. A present lockfile still runs `npm ci --dry-run`, and a stale or inconsistent lock refuses before push.
- Add the dependency-free package lock at 1.24.0, preserve package.json, update the earlier stale-lock fixture, and document public field lessons 81–85.

## Checks

- `node --test tests/field-lesson183.test.mjs`: 4 passed, 0 failed; includes fake-exec coverage and real offline npm accepting a generated lock then refusing a newly added local dependency missing from that lock.
- `npm install --package-lock-only`: passed with offline, no-audit, no-fund, ignore-scripts, isolated empty config and cache options. The generated lock contains only the root package; package.json is byte-identical to the base.
- `npm ci --dry-run`: passed with the same offline/config options.
- `npm test`: 727 tests, 725 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed; 37.600 seconds on the local machine. The first sandboxed attempt was blocked by existing tests accessing the local live-run registry and other sandbox restrictions (519 passed, 204 failed, 2 skipped); the approved run with normal local test access passed. Both logs are retained locally. No timing-flake rerun was needed.
- `npm run check`: passed package syntax, links, license, skill and example checks.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Parent re-verification after integration: all six base/output hashes matched; `npm test` 725 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped (one earlier run hit the known load flake in `cli-adapters.test.mjs:88`, not in this diff, 3/3 alone; lesson #182); `npm run check` passed; `npm ci --dry-run` passed; real stale lock (added local dependency) refused by `npm ci` with `Missing: local-extra@1.0.0 from lock file`.

- CI fix (lesson #189): the L179/L181 pre-fix proof block read `git show 3e4f4f6:…`, which fails in CI's shallow checkout and on main after squash merge. It now skips with a stated reason when that commit is absent. Full-history run: batch-k 19 passed; shallow clone: block skipped, 14 passed, 0 failed.

- Test isolation (lesson #190): `tests/ports.test.mjs` 'a non-shell claude job env…' failed only under `ship` (which exports SWARM_PORT_BASE to checks). The test now clears and restores it. `SWARM_PORT_BASE=27160 npm test`: 725 passed, 0 failed.

- macOS CI race (lesson #191): `lessons120-mutants.test.mjs` process-group cancel test probed the grandchild once, right after cancel; it failed on 2 of 3 macOS runs of one commit. It now polls up to 3 s. Mutant (kill only the direct child, not the group) still fails the test.

<!-- swarm:checks -->

## Mutation check

The new missing-lock regression failed against the unchanged pre-fix implementation on the intended assertion: `missing-lock warning must name the package.json path` (ERR_ASSERTION), with no import or setup failure. It passes with the fix.

`swarm mutants` ran the focused tests on an unmodified baseline, then killed all four changes: remove the named missing-lock warning; remove the explicit did-not-run warning; invert the lock-presence check; bypass stale-lock refusal. The last change fails both the fake-exec test and the real npm mismatch test. Result: 4 killed, 0 survived, 0 invalid. Existing adapter and ship-regression tests also passed in the complete suite.

## Speed metric

The full local suite completed in 37.600 seconds; the focused four-test suite completed in 0.535 seconds. These are observed validation times for this change, with no broader throughput claim.
